sections.title: The letter A
paragraphs: You name this letter (A) /ɑː/. Its main sound is a vowel, heard in the word (apple) /æp.əl/. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter has four sounds.

sections.title: Mouth shape
paragraphs: For the first sound, drop your jaw wide and keep your tongue low and flat. For the second sound, glide from mid front to close front. For the third sound, relax your mouth in the middle. For the fourth sound, drop your jaw deep and pull your tongue back. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake on all four sounds.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In a closed syllable, say a short sound, as in (cat) /kæt/. In an open syllable or before a silent e, say a diphthong, as in (cake) /keɪk/. A diphthong is two vowel sounds that glide together. In an unstressed syllable, say a schwa, as in (about) /ə.baʊt/. A schwa is a weak, relaxed vowel. Before an r or in special words, say a broad vowel, as in (father) /fɑː.ðər/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not replace the vowel in (hat) /hæt/ with a sound made farther back in the mouth. Keep your tongue low and push it forward toward your front teeth. In (lake) /leɪk/, do not stop on a pure flat vowel. Glide smoothly up toward the sound in (sofa) /səʊ.fə/ or close your mouth slightly at the end.
